Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for #7380: make `cgroupfs` the default validation sandbox cgroup mode and close the user-manager escape route

Planning ref: `main` @ `a5968b1c610986c0388623f2312d74948753a50b` (the integration branch metadata is empty, and the mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends sandbox_start_verified_dockerd
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers fix the scope (Q1: A, Q2: A). This plan covers exactly those: `cgroupfs` becomes the default, `auto` stays opt-in, `selfcheck` fails closed with `user_manager_reachable_from_container`, linger is cleaned up on every `cgroupfs` path, and the tests, README, agents text and changelog text are updated to match. It adds nothing else. Everything extends code that is already in `scripts/validation_harness_sandbox.sh`:
- the mode selection in `sandbox_start_verified_dockerd`;
- the root-side host-pid checks in the `docker_pidns_isolated` style;
- the existing `sandbox_fail selfcheck <reason>` exit-3 path.

Under the §6 priorities, removing the reachable user manager from the default configuration (security) outranks keeping systemd cgroup resource limits by default (performance/ops). No new workflow wiring is needed, because the daily `harness-sandbox-check` in `nightly-validation-selftest.yml` already runs the default mode.

Automation / §20 surface
- Change type: existing code only. No new script, workflow, scheduler entry or supervisor, no DB work, and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.
- Entry points that use the change unchanged:
  - `validate_process.sh` Phase 3 (`provision` / `selfcheck` / `run`);
  - `validation_refresh_runner.py` (`checked-run`);
  - the `nightly-validation-selftest.yml` `harness-sandbox-check` job (provision → checked-run → cleanup on the default mode).

- `scripts/validation_harness_sandbox.sh`
- `tests/test_validation_harness_sandbox.py`
- `README.md`

## Functions or modules to implement

1. `scripts/validation_harness_sandbox.sh`
   - **Default (line 65):** change it to `${VALIDATION_HARNESS_SANDBOX_CGROUP_MODE:-cgroupfs}`.
     - Rewrite the header comment (lines 58-64) and the comment above `sandbox_start_verified_dockerd` (lines ~470-474) to say:
       - `cgroupfs` is the default and starts no systemd user manager.
       - `auto` is opt-in. It tries a systemd user session first, and `selfcheck` then fails closed while that manager runs (#7380).
   - **Unrecognized values (lines 478-481):** log `cgroup_mode_unrecognized_using_cgroupfs` and treat the value as `cgroupfs`.
     - Restructure the second `case` so that only `auto` takes the session branch; `cgroupfs|*` sets `mode=cgroupfs`.
     - The old reason token `cgroup_mode_unrecognized_using_auto` can no longer be produced. The changelog and agents text record the new token.
   - **New helper `sandbox_release_systemd_session <user> <uid>`** (best effort, always returns 0). Place it next to `sandbox_systemd_session`. Its steps:
     - If `loginctl` exists, run `sudo -n loginctl disable-linger <user>`.
     - Run `sudo -n systemctl stop "user@<uid>.service"`.
     - Wait up to `SANDBOX_SESSION_WAIT_SECS` until `sudo -n pgrep -u <uid> -x systemd` prints nothing.
     - Log `sandbox_log provision ok systemd_user_session_released` only when a manager or linger was actually present. The helper only writes a log line; it does not fail.
   - **Call sites for the release helper.** Each one must run before the runtime dir is created or recreated, because stopping `user@<uid>` can unmount the `/run/user/<uid>` tmpfs:
     - (a) `mode=cgroupfs` chosen from the mode setting (default or unrecognized value), before the `install -d ... runtime_dir` on line 494. This clears linger left by an earlier opt-in `auto` job on a reused runner.
     - (b) the `auto` path where `sandbox_systemd_session` fails, which can leave linger enabled after `enable-linger` succeeded (line ~489).
     - (c) the probe-failure fallback (lines 504-508): after `stop_rootless_dockerd`, call the release helper, then repeat `sudo -n install -d -m 0700 -o <user> -g <group> "${runtime_dir}"`, then `start_rootless_dockerd cgroupfs`.
   - **New check function `user_manager_route_open`.** It runs as root on the host, in the host mount namespace. It returns 0 (route open) when any of these hold:
     - `sudo -n pgrep -u <uid> -x systemd`, `-x dbus-daemon` or `-x dbus-broker` finds a process. These are read from host pids, never from files the sandbox can write.
     - `sudo -n test -S "${rt}/bus"` succeeds.
     - `sudo -n find "${rt}/systemd" -xdev -type s -print -quit` prints a path.

     It returns 1 when the uid cannot be resolved (the caller then fails closed with the same reason). It returns 2 when none of the checks match.
   - **`cmd_selfcheck`:** after `docker_pidns_isolated` and before `sandbox_log selfcheck ok`, add:
     `user_manager_route_open && sandbox_fail selfcheck user_manager_reachable_from_container`
     The code must treat return 1 (uid lookup failed) as a failure too. It must not test only `rc==0`, because an unknown state must not pass. The check runs in every mode.
   - **Unchanged:** the #7349 in-namespace socket mask and the `user_manager_reachable` probe stay as defence in depth.

2. `tests/test_validation_harness_sandbox.py`
   - **`_driver`:**
     - Accept `mode: str | None`. With `None`, omit the variable from the environment so the default is tested.
     - Stub `sandbox_release_systemd_session` so it records `release $*` in the calls file.
   - **Existing #7063 tests:**
     - Keep them, passing `mode="auto"` explicitly.
     - Update the expected call lists so a release appears before every `start cgroupfs`. For example, no-session becomes `["session ...", "release ai-validation 1002", "start cgroupfs", "probe cgroupfs"]`, and the systemd→cgroupfs fallback becomes `[..., "stop", "release ...", "start cgroupfs", "probe cgroupfs"]`.
     - `test_cgroupfs_mode_never_touches_the_systemd_session` expects `["release ...", "start cgroupfs", "probe cgroupfs"]` and no `session` call.
   - **New default tests:**
     - With the variable unset, the sourced default prints `cgroupfs`.
     - `_driver(mode=None)` never calls `session`.
   - **Unrecognized value:** replace `test_an_unrecognized_cgroup_mode_is_logged_and_uses_auto` with `..._uses_cgroupfs`. It asserts `reason=cgroup_mode_unrecognized_using_cgroupfs` and no `session` call.
   - **Release helper tests** (using the `_session` / `_sourced` pattern with a sudo stub):
     - the log contains `loginctl disable-linger ai-validation` and `systemctl stop user@1002.service`;
     - it returns 0 even when `loginctl` fails.
   - **New `selfcheck` tests**, based on `test_selfcheck_fails_when_the_daemon_shares_the_host_pid_namespace`:
     - The sudo stub dispatches `pgrep` on the process name: `dockerd` gets a namespaced pid; `systemd` returns 77 → exit 3 with `phase=selfcheck outcome=fail reason=user_manager_reachable_from_container`, and the status file reads `fail selfcheck user_manager_reachable_from_container`.
     - `test -S .../bus` succeeds → same failure.
     - `find` prints a socket under `systemd/` → same failure.
     - Clean case (no manager, no sockets) → exit 0 with `selfcheck ok`.
     - Ordering contract: the `user_manager_route_open` line comes after `docker_pidns_isolated` and before `sandbox_log selfcheck ok`.
   - **Existing selfcheck stub tests:** update any `pgrep) echo 55` stub that would now also match `systemd`, so it echoes only for `dockerd`.

3. Documentation
   - **`README.md` (line 3713):** rewrite the row for `VALIDATION_HARNESS_SANDBOX_CGROUP_MODE`:
     - default `cgroupfs`;
     - `auto` is opt-in (session first, cgroupfs fallback, linger released on fallback);
     - `selfcheck` fails with `user_manager_reachable_from_container` while a user manager or its sockets exist;
     - unrecognized values log `cgroup_mode_unrecognized_using_cgroupfs`;
     - keep the probe and `container_start_failed` text.
   - **`agents.md` (line 2383, the #7063 bullet):** a direct edit that corrects existing text (§25: replace the line; no new lines, so it is within `AGENTS_MD_DIRECT_NET_ADD_MAX`). Change "enables linger…" to "in opt-in `auto` mode…", state that `cgroupfs` is the default, and change the unrecognized-value sentence.
   - **`agents.d/7349-validation-harness-pid-namespace.md`:**
     - Change "In `auto` cgroup mode the sandbox user's systemd user manager…" so it describes the mask as defence in depth for opt-in `auto`.
     - Delete the "Residual: …" sentence.
   - **`agents.d/7380-validation-harness-cgroupfs-default.md`:** a new fragment with marker `<!-- agents: section="Validation harness isolation" -->`. One bullet covering:
     - the default change;
     - `sandbox_release_systemd_session`, with its three call sites;
     - `user_manager_route_open` and its exact checks (processes `systemd` / `dbus-daemon` / `dbus-broker` for the uid, `bus`, sockets under `systemd/`);
     - the reason `user_manager_reachable_from_container` (exit 3, `harness_error`);
     - that opt-in `auto` passes only where no user manager starts;
     - why rootlesskit/containerd sockets are not counted.
   - **`changelog.d/7349-validation-harness-pid-namespace.md`:** remove "(used by the default `auto` cgroup mode)" and the "A container started through Docker can still reach that manager… set `…=cgroupfs`" sentence.
   - **`changelog.d/7380-validation-harness-cgroupfs-default.md`:** a new fragment under `<!-- changelog: security -->`, following CLAUDE.md §20 format:
     - the user-visible effect: a container can no longer start processes in the runner's PID namesp
